resolutions.researcher_notes: Old OPEC ASB2017 ref is dead (redirects to opec.org homepage; opec.org PDF paths for this ASB year no longer resolve, no live Wayback snapshot located either). Replaced with Mellitah Oil & Gas's own achievements page (operator of the Mellitah complex/pipeline, describes the 525km onshore system as in active service transporting Wafa gas) and Bonatti International's maintenance-contractor page (describes ongoing production/maintenance operations at Mellitah fed by Wafa field gas, 11 BSCM/y combined output, GreenStream export still running). Status is inferred from continuous operations described in both, not a literal 'operating' string match (expected per status-inference rule).

Mellitah O&G's achievements page states the onshore pipeline contract was 'awarded on 17/6/2002 and completed on 16/8/2004' -- directly supports ConstructionYear=2002. Also confirmed via the same operator's Arabic-language achievements page (same publisher, not counted as a second independent origin). Wikipedia's Greenstream pipeline article gives 2003 as the construction-start year for the subsea Mellitah-Gela leg specifically, which is a distinct (offshore) segment of the wider Western Libya Gas Project, so it is not treated as contradicting the 2002 onshore contract-award date; flagging the distinction rather than citing it as independent corroboration for this row. tier=medium because only one independent origin (the operator itself) speaks to this exact figure.

Mellitah O&G achievements page: onshore pipeline completed 16/8/2004. Wikipedia Greenstream pipeline article: 'Operations commenced October 1, 2004' for the wider Western Libya Gas Project that this onshore line feeds. Two independent origins agree on 2004 start. Note: Wikipedia's National Oil Corporation article (checked via search snippet) separately states the WLGP 'came online in October 2004', a third consistent source.

VALUE CONTRADICTION -- could not find any source supporting Capacity=13.00 bcm/y for this pipeline. Sources found instead: Mellitah O&G achievements page (both EN and AR) states the Western Libya Gas Project was designed for a target of ~6 BSCM/year; Bonatti International states the Mellitah complex combined output is 'about 11 BSCM/YEAR of gas'; Wikipedia's Greenstream pipeline article gives 8 bcm initial / 11 bcm expanded capacity for the subsea export line. None of the three converge on 13 bcm/y, and 13 doesn't match any combination I could construct (e.g. 6+? or domestic+export split). Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than citing a source that doesn't actually support the stated number -- flagging for the sheet maintainer that 13.00 bcm/y may need re-checking against 6 or 11 bcm/y.

VALUE CONTRADICTION -- LengthKnown=5246.00 km does not match any source found. Mellitah O&G achievements page (EN and AR) explicitly states 'The 525 Km onshore pipeline system comprises of 32" gas and 16" oil/condensates pipelines' from Wafa to Mellitah; Wikipedia's Greenstream pipeline article separately gives the Wafa-to-Mellitah onshore distance as ~530 km (and the full subsea+onshore Greenstream system as 540 km). All independent sources converge tightly around 525-530 km, an order of magnitude below the sheet's 5246.00 km. This looks like a likely data-entry artifact (e.g. a European-style decimal comma '524,6' misread/mis-keyed as '5246', or a stray digit), not a real value -- flagging for correction rather than fabricating a reference for the wrong number. Leaving UNRESOLVED; a ref for ~525 km could be added once the sheet value is corrected.

Mellitah O&G achievements page: onshore system 'comprises of 32" gas and 16" oil/condensates pipelines' -- 32in gas line matches. Wikipedia Greenstream pipeline article independently gives 'Diameter: 32 inches (810 mm)' for the same gas line. Two independent, agreeing sources.

Both sources confirm the pipeline runs from the Wafa gas field (desert, southwest Libya) to the Mellitah Complex on the Libyan coast, and both endpoints are in Libya -- supports StartLocation, EndLocation, and both CountryOrArea fields. Could NOT independently confirm the sub-national fields ('Nalut' for the start, 'Nuqat al Khams district' for the end) -- neither source, nor Wikipedia's Nuqat al Khams District article (checked directly), names these administrative units in connection with Wafa or Mellitah. tier=medium because the district-level attribution is unverified even though the facility names/country are solid.

Mellitah O&G achievements page: 'Mellitah Gas a joint venture between National Oil Corporation of Libya and ENI Italy' (confirms the two-party JV, not the exact split). Wikipedia's National Oil Corporation article states 'The Western Libyan Gas Project (WLGP) is a 50-50 joint venture between NOC and Eni,' which supplies the 50%/50% split. Wikipedia's Greenstream pipeline article is a third, consistent source ('constructed and owned by Agip Gas BV, a joint venture of...Eni and the National Oil Corporation (NOC) of Libya').
